title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the divided-power de Rham notes. It is a typed page, numbered '-135-' and marked 'IX', from the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', §11.3). The surrounding handwritten pages on the PD de Rham complex were apparently written in the same archive folder, perhaps on reused typescript. This is a guess from the page itself; I have not checked the archive.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- Setting: K is a strictly henselian discretely valued field and I its inertia group. Φ is the group of connected components of the special fibre of the Néron model of an abelian variety A_K.
- U is a free finitely generated Z_ℓ-module with an I-action; the page does not say which (presumably a Tate module attached to A_K).
- The page opens by finishing an argument: Φ (its ℓ-part, presumably) is canonically isomorphic to the torsion subgroup of H^1(I,U).
- T = Z_ℓ(1) = T_ℓ(G_m), with I acting trivially. T_n = T/nT for n = ℓ^r. D_ℓ = Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ.
- The exact sequence (11.3.3) is presumably 1 → I' → I → T → 1, where I → T is the ℓ-part of the tame character and I' has no nontrivial pro-ℓ quotient. It gives (11.3.9): H^1(I,T_n) = Hom(I,T_n) ≅ Hom(T,T_n) ≅ Z/n.
- Passing to the inductive limit over n gives H^1(I, T⊗D_ℓ) ≅ D_ℓ.
- For a finite I-Z_ℓ-module M, the Cartier dual is M' = Hom(M, T⊗D_ℓ) = Hom(M, μ_{ℓ^∞}). Cup product gives (11.3.11): H^i(I,M) ⊗ H^{1-i}(I,M') → D_ℓ.
- This is the classical perfect duality for a profinite group whose ℓ-part is Z_ℓ(1) (ℓ-cohomological dimension 1), with reference to SGA 5 I 5.
- Taking M = U_n = U/ℓ^n, so M' = U'_n with U' = Hom(U,T), and passing to the limit gives the perfect pairing (11.3.12): H^0(I, U⊗D_ℓ) × H^1(I,U') → D_ℓ. Here H^1(I,U') is a finitely generated Z_ℓ-module.
- A second limit, with transition maps ℓ^r·id (an inverse limit on the H^0 side, a colimit on the H^1 side), gives (11.3.13): H^0(I, U⊗Q_ℓ) × H^1(I, U'⊗Q_ℓ) → D_ℓ, a pairing of finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector spaces.
- Purpose: these pairings feed Grothendieck's monodromy pairing and orthogonality theorem in SGA 7 IX §11, which compare Φ with the cohomology of inertia.
errors: Minor: (11.3.13) is written with target D_ℓ. This is correct as a Pontryagin-type pairing between Q_ℓ-vector spaces (Hom_cont(Q_ℓ, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) ≅ Q_ℓ), though one could equally phrase it with target Q_ℓ.

Implicit hypothesis: the isomorphism Hom(T,T_n) → Hom(I,T_n) needs the kernel of I → T to have no nontrivial ℓ-primary abelian quotient. This holds for inertia of a strictly henselian discretely valued field (wild inertia is pro-p and the rest of tame inertia is prime-to-ℓ).

ideas.what: H^1(I,T_n) ≅ Hom(I,T_n) ≅ Z/n via the ℓ-part of the tame character, and H^1(I, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ
ideas.modern_name: tame ℓ-adic inertia cohomology / trace isomorphism for inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 I, Exp. I and IX); standard

ideas.what: Perfect cup-product duality H^i(I,M) × H^{1-i}(I,M') → Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ with Cartier dual M'
ideas.modern_name: local duality for inertia (profinite group of ℓ-cd 1)

ideas.what: Limit pairings H^0(I,U⊗D_ℓ) × H^1(I,U') → D_ℓ and its Q_ℓ version; Φ identified with the torsion of H^1(I,U)
ideas.modern_name: ingredients of Grothendieck's monodromy pairing / orthogonality theorem for Néron component groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of SGA 7 I Exposé IX §11.3, published in 1972. Its content is fully in the literature and credited to Grothendieck. It has no mathematical link to the divided-power de Rham notes that surround it in the folder.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially accurate. Note that the 'première membre' facteurs are H^0(I,U⊗D_ℓ) and H^1(I,U'); the text correctly says the second factor H^1(I,U') is of finite type over Z_ℓ.
The handwritten folio number '139' (bottom left) and the stamp '453' are archival numberings, not part of the text.
